description:
FILED s481b (2026-09-10, Opus) while measuring the critical-infrastructure
milestone (#1607).  File::Temp is on #1607's list; IO::Socket is on the
README's.

THE IDIOM.  A filehandle in perl is a GLOB, and a glob has a HASH slot, so the
classic way to hang per-handle data off a handle without a separate registry is
to use the glob as a hash.  File::Temp does it for every object it makes
(`${*$fh}{$_}` for NAME / EXLOCK / UNLINK), and IO::Handle-derived classes do
the same.

REPRODUCER (scratch/s481b/probe-glob-hash.pl), perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl:

    my $fh = \do { local *HANDLE };
    ${*$fh}{NAME}   = "/tmp/x";
    ${*$fh}{EXLOCK} = 1;
    print "name=", ${*$fh}{NAME}, " exlock=", ${*$fh}{EXLOCK}, "\n";
    print "keys=", join(",", sort keys %{*$fh}), "\n";

    perl: name=/tmp/x exlock=1 / keys=EXLOCK,NAME
    PCL : Unhandled simple-type-error â¦ Value of pcl::h in (sb-impl::gethash3 k h nil)
          is #S(p-typeglob :package #<package "MAIN"> :name "SCALAR(0x1)"),
          not a HASH-TABLE.

Note the failure MODE as much as the gap: an unhandled SBCL type error naming
an internal struct, not a trappable perl-shaped die.  Rule 12's boundary says
this is a VALUE case, so if the idiom is not going to be supported it must at
least die by name.

WHAT IT COSTS, measured (s481b).  File-Temp-0.2312-0's own suite: PCL 6 PASS /
0 PARTIAL / 5 FAIL, 46 ok / 1 not-ok against perl's 10 PASS (1 PERL-SKIP â
`lock.t`, no O_EXLOCK) and 132 ok / 0.  The files stop at their first
File::Temp object: `t/cmp.t` 1 row of 19, `t/object.t` 3 of 35, `t/seekable.t`
1 of 10, `t/fork.t` 0 of 8, `t/mktemp.t` 0 of 9, `t/posix.t` 0 of 7 â and the
backtrace of each names `(SETF P-CAST-$)` with the fd-stream as its operand
("Cannot dereference non-reference: #<fd-stream for â¦>"), i.e. the same
question asked of a real handle rather than a fresh glob.

A RELATED, DIFFERENT ONE, worth reading beside it: `require IO::Socket::INET`
dies with the same `gethash3` shape but on `Symbol::gensym`'s
`delete $$genpkg{$name}` â a SYMBOL-TABLE hash, which is
`docs/not-supported.md` "Live symbol-table hashes (%main::, %Foo::)
[DEFERRED]".  Two different hashes on the glob/stash family; do not assume one
fix covers both.

BAR: guard rows for read, write, `keys`, `delete` and `exists` on `${*$fh}{K}`
and `%{*$fh}` with perl as the oracle, on a fresh glob AND on a glob that holds
an open handle (the second is the File::Temp case and the one that reaches
`p-cast-$`).
subject: A GLOB used as per-handle storage â `${*$fh}{KEY}`, File::Temp's and IO::Handle's idiom â hits a raw SBCL type error (`gethash3 â¦ #S(p-typeglob â¦) is not a hash-table`), not a perl-shaped die.  It costs File::Temp half its suite and is the shape behind IO::Socket::INET's load failure.
